summary: v0.4.2 Phase 5C Track-aware Play mode: ALL 15 review-request items PASS on the preview URL. Play start screen renders the certification track selector with all 5 track buttons (play-track-CLF_SAA / AIF / MLA / DEA / MIXED), the description under play-track-desc updates and the choice persists to localStorage cf_play_track. Complete 3-round Play sessions for AIF, MLA, DEA, CLF/SAA, and MIXED were all playable end-to-end: each dealt hand had enough services for the min (submit-round-button enabled correctly), server scoring returned valid round breakdowns, the final summary showed the correct final-track-label ('Track: AIF' / 'Track: MLA' / 'Track: DEA' / 'Track: CLF / SAA' / 'Track: Mixed') and final-mode-label 'Mode: 3R', and play-xp-earned was exactly '+30 XP earned'. Scenarios felt domain-appropriate: AIF hands surfaced 'Generative AI Support Assistant', 'Image Moderation Service', 'Customer Feedback NLP'; MLA surfaced 'Detect Model Drift in Production', 'Feature Engineering at Scale', 'Low Latency Prediction API'; DEA surfaced 'Orchestrated ETL Workflow', 'IoT Telemetry Pipeline', 'Data Lake Foundation'. The share-play-card contains both a Track line ('Track  Mixed/AIF/...') and an XP line, confirmed via inner text. Mixed 5R completed with +50 XP and CLF/SAA 10R completed with +100 XP. Deep link /play?rounds=3&track=DEA starts a 3R DEA session directly (localStorage cf_play_track=DEA on load, Round 1/3 rendered). LearnHub practice-track-in-play link produces href '/play?track=MLA' when MLA is selected on /learn, navigates to /play, and persists cf_play_track=MLA. Leaderboard save from a completed session succeeds (name persists to /leaderboard page innerText). Leaderboard is not split by track (still 3R/5R/10R). Test Mode 15Q still awards +40 XP (regression pass). Mobile 375px shows 0 horizontal overflow on both the Play start screen (with track selector wrapped cleanly) and the Play round screen. Zero console errors and zero page errors across every flow. No em dashes observed in the new Play track UI. Match Mode was not exhaustively re-validated here (generic auto-clicker didn't find matching testids under the click-to-place UX), but it was fully green in iteration_14 and no code paths were touched in Phase 5C.

critical_code_review_comments: Play.jsx state: track is initialized once from localStorage OR cf_play_track fallback 'CLF_SAA', but ALSO overridden inside a useEffect that reads ?track=. Both paths call getSessionScenarios with the CORRECT chosen track (using the local `chosen` variable inside the effect), avoiding the classic stale-state pitfall. Nicely done.

dealRound(scenarioId, 12, 2, track) always threads the current track, so mid-session track changes cannot happen (rounds is locked once startGame(n) or the deep-link effect fires setSessionIds). Good invariant.
TRACK_LABEL map is complete for all 5 tracks and safely falls back to the raw id if unknown, so ShareResultCard and final-track-label will never render 'undefined'.
ShareResultCard receives trackLabel and xpEarned via the play kind; utils/shareResults.js now includes Track + XP lines as required.
US English, no em dashes observed in the new Play track UI copy (PLAY_TRACKS descriptions and the section heading 'Certification track' use plain hyphens and periods).

LearnHub's practice-track-in-play uses a Link with template literal `/play?track=${track}`; Play's useEffect validates the ?track value against PLAY_TRACKS and only accepts uppercase matches, so /play?track=mla, /play?track=BOGUS, or /play?track= silently fall back to localStorage or CLF_SAA. Defensive and correct.
MongoDB _id exposure was not observed in any Play/deal/session response.

Mobile 375px: no horizontal overflow on either the Play start screen (track selector wraps to 2 rows cleanly) or the Play round screen (sticky selection tray fits, scenario card breaks long strings via break-words).
Minor nit (not blocking): the play-track-desc description text uses `break-words` and `text-sm text-zinc-400` which is high enough contrast on the #0A0C0F background. No accessibility concern.
